Review Date: Reviewed in the United States on August 27, 2017
Review Body:
The hardcover book-jacket is blatant false advertising, as are the primary marketing talking points. This book’s content doesn’t place the protagonist, author J.D. Vance, in the heart of Appalachia, but instead in a working/middle class neighborhood located in Middletown, OH where he grew up. Middletown is in western Ohio, not Appalachia.

So if you were expecting an understanding of the people that live in Appalachia, and a story of that place, you’ll barely get that here.

There is some utility to this book. Given the legacy of Mr. Vance’s family leaving Appalachia poor and uneducated, he had hurdles to overcome that only the empathetic, poor, and working-class can appreciate. So I did like his story overcoming those hurdles, but I’m left still wanting a story about modern-day Appalachians.
